entities.text: DOWRY PROHIBITION ACT, 1961 BEING ARBITRARY, ERRONEOUS
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
This petition is filed by the petitioner-accused under Section 482 of Cr.P.C for quashing criminal proceedings in C.C.No.118/2023 arising out of Crime No.52/2022 registered by the Molakalmuru Police Station, Chitradurga and charge sheeted for the offence punishable under Sections 323,
498A, 504 and 506 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned HCGP for the State.
Respondent No.2 is served and unrepresented.

Brief facts leading to the case of the prosecution is that on the complaint of respondent-Police,
FIR came to be registered in Crime No.52/2022.
It is alleged that she was married to the petitioner and having two female children aged about 21 years and 17 years respectively.
They are studying in the college.
At the time of marriage, Rs.50,000/- cash, Motor Cycle, two thola Gold chain, clothes and household articles were given to the petitioner and has spent the entire marriage expenses.

4. When they were residing together, the petitioner is said to be having illicit relationship with other women, he was continuously harassing physically and mentally and even not looking after the expenses of the children and not maintaining the family and continuously abusing respondent No.2 Sri Suresha G R vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53242629/
2 in filthy language.

sentences.text: On 04.04.2022 at 10.00 a.m., the petitioner is said to have come to the house and assaulted her and abused her in filthy language and hence, the complainant went to her parents house and lodged complaint.
The Police registered NC: 2024:KHC:50697 FIR.
The FIR was withdrawn as not pressed and on filing of charge sheet, the petitioner is before this Court.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that as per allegation, the accused is said to be harassing for last five years but no such complaint is filed against him.
Alleged incident took place on 04.04.2022 but no complaint is registered on that day.
There was four days delay in lodging the complaint.
Complaint is lodged on 08.02.2022.
That apart, it is contended that the allegations are omnibus allegations which are not sustainable.
Petitioner has also filed divorce and obtained decree of divorce.
Such being the case, continuation of proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Hence, he prays to allow the petition.
6.
Per contra, learned HCGP contended that the daughters have given evidence against the petitioner for having harassing the complainant.
There are specific allegation against the petitioner and therefore, sought for dismissal of the petition.
Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and perused the material on record, relationship between the petitioner and respondent No.2 are not in dispute.
It is also not in dispute that petitioner and respondent No.2 are having two female daughters aged about 22 years and 17 years respectively, who are going to college.

The allegation against the petitioner is that five years from the date of filing the complaint, the petitioner is said to be having illicit relationship with some other lady and when the same was questioned, he used to abuse and assault the complainant physically.

It is also contended by respondent No.2 that the petitioner is not looking after the family,
not maintaining the family and not spending any amount for education expenses of the children and when the same was questioned, the petitioner asked respondent No.2 to get 10 lakhs from the parental house.
8. On this background, once again on 04.04.2022, the petitioner assaulted respondent No.2 and threatened NC: 2024:KHC:50697 to kill her.
Thereby, respondent No.2 along with her children went back to the parents house and lodged the complaint.
It is the contention of the petitioner's counsel that since five years harassment is going on.
The offence under Section 498A of IPC is harassment on the woman by the husband or the relative of the husband, is a continuing offence.
That apart on 04.04.2022, the petitioner has abused and assaulted respondent No.2 and threatened to kill her.
Thereafter, respondent No.2 went to her parents house and admittedly, lodged complaint on 08.04.2022.
Of course, there is four days delay in lodging the complaint.
Background of this petitioner was that he was a practicing Advocate in Molakalmuru Taluk and respondent No.2 is wife.
Even if she go to the Police Station, the Police may not entertain the complaint and register FIR immediately.

9. As seen from the records in the matrimonial case, where the petitioner obtained the decree of divorce and respondent counsel retired from the case and exparte NC: 2024:KHC:50697 decree of Sri Suresha G R vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53242629/
3 divorce has been granted, which shows that respondent No.2 is not able to contest the matter because she is already abandoned by the petitioner and not maintained by the petitioner.

sentences.text: On perusal of the statement of the K.S.Ananda, brother of the complainant, statements of Meghana G.S. and Mahima G.S., who are the daughters of petitioner and respondent No.2, it is observed that they have also given statement against the petitioner for having harassing respondent No.2, demanding dowry and assault made by the petitioner.
Apart from that, parents of respondent No.2 have also given statement against the petitioner.
10. Such being the case, I am of the view that this is not a fit case for quashing the criminal proceedings.
The petition is devoid of merits.
Accordingly, petition is dismissed.
Any observations made by this Court shall not be influenced by the trial Court.
